implementation_notes: Optional chaining ?. and nullish coalescing ?? are language operators: a property access or call on null/undefined short-circuits to undefined, and ?? supplies a default while preserving falsy-but-present values such as 0 and the empty string. The plural focus is Array.prototype.flatMap, which maps each element and flattens one level, so a callback returning an empty array yields zero targets and a single-element array yields one. These operators replace the classic optic structure; because JavaScript has no type-level absence, present-versus-absent stays a runtime convention that should be documented.
pitfalls: ?. protects only the access it is written on: (a?.b).c throws again, and a single missing ?. in a long chain still produces a TypeError.
?? treats only null and undefined as absent while || also replaces 0, the empty string and false, so the wrong choice silently drops valid values.
flatMap is synchronous: a per-target asynchronous update needs Promise.all, for await or a helper index loop instead.
